author: LuciferYang
body:
Pushed a review follow-up (d59782f6c) with two changes worth calling out.

Cleanup now skips any id the current manifest references. `new_id != old_id` is evaluated per entry, so on its own it cannot exclude a `new_id` that happens to be another entry's live id, and `IndexRemapper` / `RemappedIndex` are public — a caller-supplied remapper can report an already-committed uuid. Both filters stay, because an index reported as kept is referenced by the snapshot the remapper planned against, which can be older than the current manifest; neither one subsumes the other.

The index list is read inside the cleanup rather than on the way to the commit. Reading it earlier would add index IO to a path that has none today (stable row ids without deferred remap), and a transient failure there would fail a compaction that would otherwise succeed, stranding the very data files the failure path exists to remove. A read failure now skips deletion instead.

One correction to the description above: I attributed the fragment-reuse orphans to #7207, but that issue reports stranded IVF_PQ index generations from the remap path. The fragment-reuse arm is a second site with the same shape, not something #7207 observed. The comment making that claim is gone.

author: LuciferYang
body:
Closing: superseded by #7722.

This PR deletes the transaction's `_indices/{uuid}/` directories when `apply_commit` returns `Err`, on the premise that `Err` proves the manifest was never published. #7722 removed that premise. A commit whose manifest is verified to have landed still surfaces as `Err` when the handler's `propagate_commit_error_after_success()` is `true`, which is the trait default (`lance-table/src/io/commit.rs:801`) and is inherited by `ExternalManifestCommitHandler` and every `CommitLock`-based handler. On those deployments this cleanup would delete index directories the committed manifest references. The `load_indices()` guard I added does not catch it: `apply_commit` exits with `?`, so the handle still holds the pre-commit manifest and the just-committed uuid is absent from the guard's set.

Closing rather than rebasing, for two reasons beyond the premise.

The safe gate would be a hand-rolled three-clause predicate reconstructing a state the commit layer already computed, where missing one handler flag corrupts a table. And collection at this level is structurally incomplete: a rebase mints additional fragment-reuse uuids inside the retry loop (`io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs` `finish_rewrite`) that `commit_compaction` never sees.

The conclusion #7722 reached for data files does not carry over unchanged, though. Its decisive argument is cross-call replay: `RewriteResult` is serializable, so a replayed compaction carries the same file paths the first, ambiguously-landed attempt committed, while the replay's own transaction verifies as foreign. Confirmed-not-committed is therefore not sufficient for data files. Index ids are different — they are minted fresh inside each `commit_compaction` call and appear nowhere in `RewriteResult`, so a replay can never collide with previously landed ones, and a verified-not-committed signal is sufficient for them.

The right place is `commit_transaction`'s verified-loss arms, next to the existing `cleanup_transaction_file` calls, where ownership is already proven and the transaction itself carries `rewritten_indices[].new_id` and `frag_reuse_index.uuid`. That also reaches the rebase-minted fragment-reuse directories this PR cannot see, and extends to `CreateIndex`, which writes `_indices/{uuid}/` before committing with no cleanup on failure today — the IVF_PQ orphan shape #7207 actually reports. I will open that separately.
